rag.name: List.Vector.tail_map
rag.content:
@[simp]
theorem tail_map {β : Type*} (v : Vector α (n + 1)) (f : α → β) :
    (v.map f).tail = v.tail.map f := by
  obtain ⟨a, v', h⟩ := Vector.exists_eq_cons v
  rw [h, map_cons, tail_cons, tail_cons]

rag.name: List.Vector.get_zero
rag.content:
@[simp]
theorem get_zero : ∀ v : Vector α n.succ, get v 0 = head v
  | ⟨_ :: _, _⟩ => rfl

informal_statement: For any vector `v` of length `n + 2`, the second element of `v` is equal to the first element of the tail of `v`.
informal_proof:
Consider an arbitrary vector `v` of length `n + 2`. 
To show that `v.get 1` is equal to `v.tail.head`, we can use the properties of vectors and their tail access operations.
By rewriting the expression `v.get 1` using the definition of vector access and tail access, we observe that both expressions refer to the same element in the vector. This completes the proof.

id.name: List.Vector.get_one
id.content:
lemma get_one {α : Type*} {n} (v : Vector α (n + 2)) : v.get 1 = v.tail.head := by
  rw [←Vector.get_zero, Vector.get_tail_succ]; rfl
